prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer seated atop a tractor looking down and right over a plowed field, with the steering wheel at the bottom-left and the right canopy support pole at the upper-right brightest within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m). The blue tractor hood, exhaust pipe, right side-view mirror, and right fender with its grab handle sit at intermediate distances (~0.8–2.5 m), while the ground slopes smoothly from ~2 m near the right wheel to over 15 m at the top edge. Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns their head to the right, shifting the steering wheel and hood partially out of the left edge of the view while bringing the right fender and canopy frame fully into the right foreground. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly isolates the thin mirror bracket, grab handle, and canopy strut from the cluttered soil background and shows the continuous ground plane gradient. However, the map is unreliable on the reflective mirror surface (treating it as a flat plane rather than a reflection of the wearer) and completely misses the distant standing person (~10–15 m ahead in the field, facing away/sideways and not looking at the wearer) who merges into the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map captures only the left portion of the tractor (steering wheel, hood, exhaust pipe, and mirror) while leaving the right fender, plowed field, and people unsegmented in black. Across the five frames, as the camera turns right, the purple mask on the left shrinks and shifts further left as the tractor hood moves partly out of view, and a yellow mask appears on the upper-right canopy strut in frame 4. While the map successfully outlines the sharp silhouette of the side-view mirror and exhaust assembly against the textured dirt, it is highly unreliable in both classification and completeness. It mislabels the agricultural tractor as a 'motorcycle' across all frames, misclassifies the side-view mirror in frame 1 as a 'traffic light' and the canopy frame in frame 4 as a 'bicycle', and leaves thin struts and the mirror bracket disconnected. Furthermore, it completely fails to segment the camera wearer's hands on the steering wheel (~0.4 m away), the wearer's reflection in the mirror, the right fender (~0.8–1.2 m away), and the distant person standing in the upper field (~10–15 m away, ~8–13 m beyond the tractor nose).
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, providing no spatial detections despite multiple human figures and body parts visible in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the camera wearer's left and right hands grip and adjust the steering wheel at the bottom-left within immediate reach (~0.4–0.5 m) in frames 1, 4, and 5, partially occluded by the wheel rim and the lower frame boundary. The camera wearer's torso and head (facing forward toward the tractor controls) are also visible as a reflection inside the right side-view mirror (~1.2 m away), and a second person stands upright in the distant field (~10–15 m ahead to the upper-right, facing sideways/away and not looking toward the camera wearer) in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. Across the sequence, as the camera turns right, the distant person shifts from the upper-left of the field in frame 1 to the upper-right in frame 5, while the wearer's right hand moves onto the bottom of the wheel in frames 4 and 5. The pose map is entirely unreliable here, failing to detect truncated egocentric hands at the frame bottom, reflected bodies in the mirror, or small distant figures against the soil.
